Work with ASCII and UTF-8 strings in Move.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/move-basics/string.html

exercises.name: tx_context1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_proposal: Set deadline = tx_context::epoch(ctx) + duration, store proposal
2. sign_proposal: vector::contains() checks duplicates, vector::push_back() adds signer + epoch
3. execute_proposal: Check vector::length(&signers) >= required AND current_epoch <= deadline
4. verify_time_window: Loop signature_epochs, track min/max, return max - min

Key Pattern: tx_context provides epoch for time-based logic & sender for auth

Real Use: DAO proposals with expiration dates & signature tracking
exercises.description:
Exercise: Transaction Context - Multi-Sig Timestamp System

Build a multi-signature system that tracks when each signer approves,
with time windows for validity using transaction context.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/transaction-context.html

exercises.name: tx_context2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. mint_nft: Store created_epoch = tx_context::epoch(), birth_time = epoch_timestamp_ms()
2. transfer_nft: Update current_owner, transfer_count++, last_transfer_epoch = current
3. evolve_nft: Age = current - created_epoch. Stages: 0-4→0, 5-9→1, 10-19→2, 20+→3
4. power_up: Check last_transfer_epoch < current (prevent spam), update power

Key Pattern: Epoch tracking enables dynamic NFT evolution over time

Real Use: Tamagotchi-style NFTs that grow with age & user interaction
exercises.description:
Exercise: Transaction Context - Dynamic NFT Evolution

Create NFTs that evolve based on transaction context (epoch, transfers, ownership time).
NFTs "age" and change attributes over time using epoch tracking.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/transaction-context.html

exercises.name: tx_context3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_escrow: Store locked_until_epoch, use tx_context::fresh_object_address() for unique ID
2. release_funds: Check current_epoch >= locked_until AND is_approved, transfer funds
3. cancel_escrow: Only if current_epoch < locked_until - 1 (early cancellation window)
4. approve_release: Verify sender == approver, set is_approved = true

Key Pattern: fresh_object_address() generates unique IDs using tx context

Real Use: Freelancer payments - funds locked until milestone approval + time
exercises.description:
Exercise: Transaction Context - Time-Locked Escrow

Build an escrow system with time locks using epoch-based constraints.
Use fresh_object_address for unique escrow IDs and epoch timing for releases.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/transaction-context.html

exercises.name: init1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. fun init(ctx: &mut TxContext): Create Registry, share_object() makes it public
2. register: vector::contains() checks duplicates, vector::push_back() adds user
3. Create RegistrationBadge with registration_number = total_registrations++

Key Pattern: init() runs ONCE during publish - perfect for shared state setup

Real Use: Global name registries (ENS, Sui NS) that need single initialization
exercises.description:
Exercise: Module Initializer - Registry System

Build a global registry system that initializes once when the module is published.
The registry tracks all users and their registration status.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/module-initializer.html

exercises.name: init2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. fun init(witness: INIT2, ctx): Witness auto-provided, create Treasury + MintCap
2. mint: Check remaining_mints > 0, amount <= (total - circulating), decrement/increment
3. burn: Unpack token, decrement circulating_supply, object::delete(id)

Key Pattern: init witness + MintCap = controlled token supply

Real Use: Fixed-supply tokens (21M Bitcoin) with limited minting capability
exercises.description:
Exercise: Module Initializer - Token System

Create a token system where the initial supply is minted during module initialization.
The publisher gets special minting privileges through initialization.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/module-initializer.html

exercises.name: init3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. fun init: Create GameWorld + ZoneDirectory + 3 starter zones, share_object() all
2. join_zone: Check vector::length() < max_players, !vector::contains(player), push_back
3. leave_zone: Loop to find index, vector::remove() deletes player
4. Store zone IDs: object::uid_to_address(&zone.id) or uid_to_inner()

Key Pattern: Complex initialization - multiple shared objects, starter data

Real Use: MMO game worlds with pre-configured zones at launch
exercises.description:
Exercise: Module Initializer - Game World Setup

Initialize a complex game world with multiple interconnected objects.
This demonstrates how init can set up an entire ecosystem in one go.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/module-initializer.html

exercises.name: capability1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_system: Create System + AdminCap, share_object(system), transfer cap to owner
2. grant_admin/moderator: Check !is_locked, create cap, increment count, transfer to recipient
3. ban_user_with_moderator: Require _cap: &ModeratorCap parameter (proves auth!)
4. lock_system: Set is_locked = true (no more capability grants)

Key Pattern: Capability object = permission token. No cap? Can't call function!

Real Use: Discord-style role system - admins grant moderator caps to trusted users
exercises.description:
Exercise: Capability Pattern - Admin System

Build a role-based access control system using the Capability pattern.
Different capabilities grant different permissions.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/capability.html

exercises.name: capability2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_treasury: Create Treasury + MasterKey, share treasury, transfer key to CEO
2. withdraw_with_master: Check balance >= amount (NO LIMIT for master!)
3. withdraw_with_manager: Check amount <= withdrawal_limit AND balance >= amount
4. grant_*: Requires &MasterKey, create cap with custom limits, transfer
5. Return WithdrawalReceipt with tx_context::epoch() for audit trail

Key Pattern: Tiered capabilities - MasterKey > ManagerKey > ClerkKey

Real Use: Company treasury - CEO unlimited, CFO limited, accountants view-only
exercises.description:
Exercise: Capability Pattern - Treasury Management

Build a multi-level treasury system where different capabilities
grant different spending limits and permissions.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/capability.html

exercises.name: capability3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_dao: Store dao_id = object::uid_to_inner(&dao.id), create MemberCaps with voting_power
2. vote_with_*: Check status == 0 (Active), !vector::contains(voter), add voting_power to yes/no
3. finalize_proposal: If yes_votes >= threshold → status=1 (Passed), else status=2 (Rejected)
4. delegate_vote: Create DelegateCap with combined voting_power from multiple members

Key Pattern: Capability carries voting power - enables delegation & compound voting

Real Use: DAOs like Nouns - members delegate voting power to trusted representatives
exercises.description:
Exercise: Capability Pattern - Governance System

Build a DAO-style governance system where voting capabilities
represent different voting powers and proposal creation rights.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/capability.html

exercises.name: time_lock
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_time_lock: clock::timestamp_ms(&clock) gets current time, add lock_duration_ms
2. Store coin as Balance: coin::into_balance(coin), store value = coin::value(&coin)
3. withdraw: Check clock::timestamp_ms() >= unlock_time AND !is_withdrawn
4. Restore coin: balance::split() → coin::from_balance()

Key Pattern: Clock object = trustless on-chain timestamps (vs tx_context::epoch)

Real Use: Savings accounts - "lock 1000 SUI for 6 months, earn 5% APY"
exercises.description:
Exercise: Epoch and Time - Time-Locked Vault

Build a time-locked vault where funds can't be withdrawn until a future time.
Similar to an escrow or savings account with withdrawal restrictions.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/epoch-and-time.html

exercises.name: vesting
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_vesting: coin::into_balance() converts Coin → Balance, store total amount
2. calculate_vested_amount: Linear formula = total * (elapsed / duration)
   - Before start: return 0
   - After end: return total_amount
3. claim_vested: claimable = vested - claimed, balance::split(&mut balance, claimable)

Key Pattern: Linear vesting = tokens unlock proportionally over time

Real Use: Employee stock options - 4 year vest, 1 year cliff (25% after year 1)
exercises.description:
Exercise: Epoch and Time - Token Vesting Schedule

Build a linear token vesting schedule where tokens unlock gradually over time.
Used for employee compensation, investor unlocks, or founder shares.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/epoch-and-time.html

exercises.name: auction
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. calculate_current_price: Linear decrease = starting - (price_drop * elapsed / duration)
   - Cap at reserve_price (minimum)
2. buy: Check started, !ended, !sold. Get current_price, check payment >= price
3. Handle overpayment: coin::split() exact amount, refund extra with coin::from_balance()
4. Store proceeds: balance::join(&mut auction.proceeds, payment_balance)

Key Pattern: Price decreases over time until someone buys (self-adjusting market)

Real Use: NFT drops (Azuki) - starts at 10 ETH, drops to 0.5 ETH over 24h
exercises.description:
Exercise: Epoch and Time - Dutch Auction

Build a Dutch auction where price decreases over time until someone buys.
Used for NFT sales, IPO pricing, and fair price discovery.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/epoch-and-time.html

exercises.name: table_basics
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_registry: table::new() creates empty Table<address, UserProfile>, share_object()
2. register_user: Check !table::contains(), table::add() inserts key-value
3. update_user: table::borrow_mut() gets &mut reference, modify fields directly
4. remove_user: Verify owner, table::remove() returns value and deletes entry

Key Pattern: Table = on-chain HashMap with copy/drop types (address → struct)

Why Table vs Vector? O(1) lookup by key vs O(n) search. Perfect for registries!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Collections - Table (User Registry)

Build a user registry using Table to store usernames and profiles.
Table is ideal for key-value storage with copy/drop types.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/collections.html

exercises.name: bag_basics
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_wallet: bag::new() creates empty Bag, transfer to owner
2. deposit: bag::add<T>(key, value) stores ANY type - Coin<SUI>, Coin<USDC>, NFTs
3. withdraw: bag::borrow_mut<Coin<T>>() gets mutable ref, coin::split() for partial
4. remove_asset: bag::remove<T>() returns full value, transfer to owner

Key Pattern: Bag = heterogeneous storage (different value types, same key type)

Why Bag? Multi-currency wallet: "SUI" → Coin<SUI>, "USDC" → Coin<USDC> in ONE bag!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Collections - Bag (Multi-Asset Wallet)

Build a multi-asset wallet using Bag to store different coin types.
Bag allows heterogeneous storage with different value types.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/collections.html

exercises.name: object_table
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_collection: object_table::new() creates ObjectTable<u64, NFT>, share it
2. mint_nft: Check max_supply, create NFT with new UID, object_table::add(id, nft)
3. transfer_nft: object_table::remove() takes ownership, transfer::public_transfer(nft, recipient)
4. burn_nft: Remove, unpack struct, object::delete(uid)

Key Pattern: ObjectTable stores objects WITH UIDs (vs Table with copy/drop types)

Real Use: NFT collections - each NFT needs UID for ownership tracking
exercises.description:
Exercise: Collections - ObjectTable (NFT Collection)

Build an NFT collection manager using ObjectTable to store NFTs.
ObjectTable stores objects as values, maintaining their UIDs.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/collections.html

exercises.name: object_bag
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_vault: object_bag::new() creates ObjectBag, set is_locked = false
2. deposit: Wrap value in Asset<T> with new UID, object_bag::add(key, asset)
3. withdraw: Check !is_locked, object_bag::remove(), unpack Asset, object::delete(uid), return value
4. lock/unlock: Toggle is_locked boolean (only owner)

Key Pattern: ObjectBag = Bag + ObjectTable = heterogeneous objects WITH UIDs

Why ObjectBag? Store NFT + Coin<SUI> + GameItem all in ONE vault with different types!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Collections - ObjectBag (Mixed Asset Vault)

Build a vault that stores different types of objects using ObjectBag.
ObjectBag combines Bag's heterogeneity with ObjectTable's object storage.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/collections.html

exercises.name: wrapper_basics
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. wrap_gift: Create GiftBox<T> with new UID, store inner object + recipient + message
2. unwrap_gift: Check sender == recipient, unpack wrapper, object::delete(uid), return inner
3. peek_message: Read-only access to message without unwrapping (check recipient first)

Key Pattern: Wrapper adds access control - only recipient can unwrap inner object

Real Use: NFT gifts - sender wraps with message, only recipient can unwrap & claim
exercises.description:
Exercise: Wrapper Type - Gift Box System

Build a gift wrapping system using wrapper types for object protection.
Wrappers control access and add functionality to wrapped objects.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/wrapper-type-pattern.html

exercises.name: authorization_wrapper
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. wrap_document: Create AuthWrapper with authorized_approvers list, empty approvals vector
2. approve_document: Check sender in authorized_approvers, !in approvals, push sender
3. finalize_document: Check vector::length(approvals) >= required, unpack wrapper, return doc

Key Pattern: Wrapper enforces multi-sig approval before access (shared object pattern)

Real Use: Legal contracts - 3 of 5 board members must approve before execution
exercises.description:
Exercise: Wrapper Type - Document Authorization System

Build a document approval system using wrappers for authorization.
Wrappers can enforce multi-step approval workflows.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/wrapper-type-pattern.html

exercises.name: dynamic_fields1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. add_metadata: Check !df::exists_(), wrap in MetadataValue struct, df::add(&mut uid, key, value)
2. get_metadata: Verify df::exists_(), df::borrow() gets immutable ref, return value field
3. update_metadata: df::borrow_mut() gets mutable ref, modify value field directly
4. remove_metadata: df::remove() returns MetadataValue, extract value field

Key Pattern: Dynamic Fields add runtime key-value pairs WITHOUT modifying struct definition

Real Use: NFT metadata - add "artist", "description", "royalty" fields after mint
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Fields - Metadata System

Build a metadata system using dynamic fields to attach flexible data to objects.
Dynamic fields allow adding key-value pairs at runtime without modifying struct definitions.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-fields.html

exercises.name: dynamic_fields2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. add_stat: Check !df::exists_(), verify value <= max_value, df::add() with StatAttribute
2. increase_stat: df::borrow_mut() gets &mut ref, value++, clamp to max_value
3. decrease_stat: df::borrow_mut(), value--, ensure >= 0
4. add_counter: df::add() with CounterAttribute { count: 0 }
5. increment_counter: df::borrow_mut(), count++

Key Pattern: Dynamic Fields store copy/drop types - perfect for numeric stats

Real Use: RPG character stats - strength, agility, mana that level up over time
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Fields - Attribute System

Build an advanced attribute system using dynamic fields with numeric values.
Store different types of attributes (stats, counters, flags) on game items.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-fields.html

exercises.name: dynamic_object_fields1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. attach: dof::exists_() checks if slot taken, verify owner, dof::add() attaches Attachment
2. detach: dof::remove<String, Attachment>() removes and RETURNS object (UID intact!)
3. get_attachment: dof::borrow() for immutable read
4. get_attachment_mut: dof::borrow_mut() for modifying attached object

Key Pattern: DOF stores OBJECTS as values - they keep their UID (vs DF which stores data)

Real Use: Attach mods to weapons, upgrades to items - detach and transfer separately!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Object Fields - Attachment System

Build an attachment system using dynamic object fields to attach objects to other objects.
Dynamic object fields store objects as values, maintaining their UIDs and ownership.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-object-fields.html

exercises.name: dynamic_object_fields2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. attach_component: Check !exists, verify owner & level>0, dof::add(), increment component_count
2. detach_component: Verify exists & owner, dof::remove(), decrement component_count
3. upgrade_component: dof::borrow_mut() gets component, update level (max 10)
4. total_component_power: Check common slots ("engine", "shield"), sum level * 10

Key Pattern: Multiple DOF on same object (engine + shield + weapon all on one ship!)

Pro Tip: Component count tracked separately from DOF - useful for UI/stats!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Object Fields - Component System

Build a component system where objects can have multiple child objects attached.
Use dynamic object fields to create flexible object hierarchies.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-object-fields.html

exercises.name: dynamic_collections1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_registry: table::new() creates empty Table<address, UserProfile>, share it
2. register_user: table::contains() checks if user exists, table::add() adds profile
3. add_custom_field: table::borrow_mut() gets profile, df::add() attaches custom data
4. get_custom_field: table::borrow() reads profile, df::borrow() reads custom field

Key Pattern: Table stores fixed schema (username), Dynamic Fields add flexible metadata (GitHub link, Twitter)
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Collections - User Profiles with Metadata

Build a user profile system combining Table for storage with Dynamic Fields for custom metadata.
This pattern combines structured storage (Table) with flexible custom attributes (Dynamic Fields).

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-collections.html

exercises.name: dynamic_collections2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_game: object_table::new() for ObjectTable<u64, Character>, share game world
2. create_character: Create Character with UID, object_table::add(), return character ID
3. attach_equipment: object_table::borrow_mut() gets character, dof::add() attaches gear
4. detach_equipment: dof::remove() removes and RETURNS equipment (UID stays intact!)
5. get_character_power: Check if slots exist (weapon/armor/accessory), sum their power

Key Pattern: ObjectTable stores Character NFTs, DOF attaches Equipment NFTs to characters
exercises.description:
// Exercise: Dynamic Collections - Game Character System

Build a game character system combining ObjectTable for character storage with Dynamic Object Fields for equipment.
This pattern allows characters to be objects while maintaining flexible equipment attachment.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-collections.html

exercises.name: dynamic_collections3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_portfolio: bag::new() creates Bag (holds mixed types!), transfer to owner
2. add_asset: bag::add<T>() stores ANY type - Coin<SUI>, Coin<USDC>, NFTs all in ONE Bag
3. tag_asset: df::add() on portfolio UID tags assets ("DeFi", "NFT", "Gaming")
4. get_asset_tag: df::borrow() reads tag, filter by category

Key Pattern: Bag = mixed types storage, Dynamic Fields = categorization layer

Why Bag? Table requires same value type. Bag allows Coin<SUI> + Coin<USDC> + NFT together!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Dynamic Collections - Multi-Asset Portfolio

Build a portfolio system using Bag to store heterogeneous assets (coins, NFTs, etc).
Bag allows mixing different types of values in a single collection with dynamic field access.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/dynamic-collections.html

exercises.name: generic_witness1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_registry: vec_map::empty() for registered types, share registry
2. register_type<T>: type_name::with_original_ids<T>() gets type, vec_map::insert() registers it
3. update_metadata<T>: Requires TypeCapability<T> (proves ownership), vec_map::get_mut() updates

Key Pattern: Witness proves "I own type T" → Only that module can register/update T

Why Witness? Prevents anyone from registering fake "YourToken" - only YOUR module can!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Generic Witness - Type-Safe Container Factory

Build a container factory using generic witness pattern for type-safe initialization.
Generic witness ensures containers can only be created with valid witness types.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/witness-pattern.html

exercises.name: generic_witness2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. create_marketplace<W>: Consume witness W, create MarketplaceAuthority<W> (has store!)
2. create_item<T>: Requires &MarketplaceAuthority<T> (reusable badge), creates Item<T>
3. list_item: vec_map::insert() tracks price, transfer item to marketplace
4. buy_item: Check payment >= price, vec_map::remove(), transfer payment & item

Key Pattern: Authority<W> can be TRANSFERRED (delegate to employee) and REUSED (mint multiple items)

 vs OTW: One-Time Witness = use once. Generic Witness with store = transfer & reuse!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Generic Witness - Delegatable Authorization

Build an authorization system using transferable witness objects for delegatable access control.
Witness objects can be transferred to delegate authority while maintaining type safety.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/witness-pattern.html

exercises.name: generic_witness3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. verify_type<W>: Consumes witness, returns VerificationProof<W> (has copy!)
2. issue_certificate<T>: Requires proof, increment registry, create Certificate<T> NFT
3. create_verified_container<T>: Requires proof, wraps value T in VerifiedContainer<T>
4. upgrade_verification: Requires Certificate<T> (authority) to upgrade level

Key Pattern: Witness → Proof → Certificate. Each step proves previous completion!

Real Use: Luxury goods verification - only verified Rolex can be containerized & sold
exercises.description:
Exercise: Generic Witness - Supply Chain Verification

Build a supply chain system using witness proofs for verification and tracking.
Witness proofs guarantee that verification steps have been completed before allowing operations.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/witness-pattern.html

exercises.name: witness1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_treasury: coin::into_balance() converts Coin → Balance, set is_initialized=true, share_object()
2. mint: Check is_initialized, balance::split() withdraws, coin::from_balance() creates Coin
3. Return Coin + Token NFT to sender

Key Pattern: WITNESS1 can ONLY be created during module init - guarantees single initialization!

Why OTW? Prevents double-initialization attacks. Treasury can't be created twice!
exercises.description:
Exercise: One-Time Witness (OTW) - Token System

Build a token system using One-Time Witness pattern to ensure single initialization.
OTW ensures that certain operations can only happen once per module deployment.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/one-time-witness.html

exercises.name: witness2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_registry: Empty vector, admin=sender, is_initialized=true, share_object()
2. register: vector::contains() checks duplicates, vector::push_back() adds user
3. remove_registration: vector::swap_remove() removes by index (admin only!)

Key Pattern: WITNESS2 struct name MUST match module name (witness2 → WITNESS2)

Why OTW? Ensures global registry created once. No one can create fake registry!
exercises.description:
Exercise: One-Time Witness (OTW) - Registry System

Build a global registry system using OTW to ensure single initialization.
The registry tracks all registered entities and can only be created once.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/one-time-witness.html

exercises.name: witness3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_system: admin=sender, is_initialized=true, is_locked=false, share_object()
2. grant_admin_cap: Verify admin & !is_locked, create AdminCap, track in vector, transfer
3. revoke_admin_cap: Verify admin, vector::swap_remove() removes capability
4. lock_system: Set is_locked=true (no more admins can be added!)

Key Pattern: OTW initialization → Grant capabilities → Lock system

Why Lock? Prevents admin from adding more admins after launch (security!)
exercises.description:
Exercise: One-Time Witness (OTW) - Capability System

Build a capability system using OTW to ensure single admin capability creation.
The system issues admin capabilities that can only be created once during initialization.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/one-time-witness.html

exercises.name: publisher1
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_collection: package::claim() gets Publisher, display::new<ArtNFT>() creates Display
2. Set fields: display::add() for each ("name" → "{name}", "image_url" → "{image_url}")
3. display::update_version() publishes changes
4. mint_nft: Increment minted, create ArtNFT with edition number, transfer to recipient

Key Pattern: Publisher proves ownership → Display defines wallet appearance

 Real Magic: Set Display ONCE, ALL NFTs look beautiful in every Sui wallet automatically!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Publisher Pattern - NFT Collection with Display

Build an NFT collection using Publisher pattern to set display metadata.
Publisher proves package ownership and allows you to define how NFTs appear in wallets.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/publisher.html

exercises.name: publisher2
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_game: package::claim(), display::new<GameWeapon>() with rich description
2. Combine fields in description: "Level {level} {weapon_type} with {attack_power} attack"
3. forge_weapon: Validate rarity (1-4), create with level=1, increment legendary_count if rare
4. level_up_weapon: Verify owner, level++, attack_power += 10%

Key Pattern: Display templates can COMBINE multiple fields for dynamic descriptions

Pro Tip: Image URL can be dynamic: ".../{weapon_type}_{rarity}.png" shows different images!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Publisher Pattern - Game Assets with Display

Build a game asset system using Publisher to create rich metadata displays.
Learn how Display makes your game items look professional in wallets and marketplaces.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/publisher.html

exercises.name: publisher3
exercises.hint:
Quick Start:
1. init_verification_system: package::claim(), create Display for BOTH types (Item + Certificate)
2. issue_certificate: Requires &Publisher (proves authority), create Certificate NFT
3. create_verified_item: option::some(certificate) attaches proof, transfer item
4. transfer_verified_item: option::extract() removes certificate, re-attach to new item

Key Pattern: Publisher enables transfer policies & verification - only verified items can trade

Real Use: Marketplaces check Publisher to verify authenticity before allowing sales!
exercises.description:
Exercise: Publisher Pattern - Package Verification & Transfer Policies

Build a package verification system using Publisher to prove authenticity.
Learn how Publisher enables transfer policies and package ownership verification.

Stuck? Check out: https://move-book.com/programmability/publisher.html
